methodological_rigor.justification: The study uses a multi-modal, multi-cohort design (discovery D1 n=38 plus seven validation cohorts totaling ~500 scRNA-seq and ~1,582 survival patients) with appropriate statistical frameworks (Dirichlet regression with log-likelihood testing, Wilcoxon with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction, moderated t-tests, Moran's I for pseudotime). Clonal tracking combining BCR-seq with scRNA-seq-based isotype inference is methodologically strong and complements orthogonal assays (mIHC, seromics, ELISpot). However, several key analyses rely on small subgroups: bulk RNA-seq uses only 4 responders vs 8 non-responders; single-cell BCR-seq includes only 2R vs 4NR (expanded to 8R/14NR by inference); spatial transcriptomics 4R vs 3NR; mIHC 6R vs 10-11NR; and ELISpot essentially one patient per group. No power calculation is reported, blinding of pathological response assessment is not described, and FDR thresholds vary across analyses (0.05 vs 0.2), weakening statistical consistency. The observational discovery design (no randomization) limits causal inference, though triangulation across independent cohorts partly mitigates this.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a correlative biomarker study nested in prospective neoadjuvant trials (NCT03916627) with validation across additional prospective cohorts including randomized phase 3 data (IMbrave150, POPLAR, OAK) and TCGA; the overall body of evidence is best classified as individual cohort/biomarker (Oxford 2b). Clinical relevance is high: the work identifies a candidate predictive biomarker (IgG1+ PC signature and anti-CTA seroreactivity) for ICB response in HCC, with validation extending to melanoma and NSCLC, and endpoints include pathological response and OS. Translational implications are concrete, including serological pre-treatment stratification, companion diagnostic development, and rationale for CTA-vaccine plus ICB combinations and IL-6/TNF/ERN1 modulation. Findings are not yet practice-changing but inform near-term translational development.

reporting_quality.justification: REMARK is the most applicable checklist given the biomarker/prognostic focus (STROBE is also partly relevant for the cohort components). Patient and cohort descriptions, assay details (ELISA, ELISpot, seromics, scRNA-seq/BCR-seq, spatial transcriptomics, mIHC), IRB approvals, and trial registrations are reported in reasonable detail. However, several REMARK items are weakly covered: no explicit biomarker pre-specification, limited reporting of patient flow/attrition, no CONSORT-like diagram, inconsistent FDR thresholds, no multivariable adjustment for confounders in survival analyses, and no detailed handling of missing data. Data availability is strong—dbGaP (phs001680.v1.p1, PRJNA489548), GEO (GSE151530), SRA (GSE238264), EGA (EGAS00001007547), and a Zenodo deposit (10.5281/zenodo.17393774) are cited—though analytical code specifics and container reproducibility details are not fully described in this blinded version.

novelty_literature.justification: The study provides a meaningful advance by linking IgG1-class-switched plasma cells and CTA-specific IgG1 seroreactivity (particularly NY-ESO-1, MAGE-A, GAGE7, PRAME) to ICB response, with multi-omic clonal tracking across tumor/adjacent liver/draining lymph node and dynamic on-treatment changes. Prior work has established B cell/TLS/PC prognostic significance (Helmink, Petitprez, Patil, Cabrita) and NY-ESO-1 antibody-ICB associations (Yuan 2008/2011, Ohue 2019), so the isotype-resolved, clonally expanded IgG1 PC phenotype plus the serology-cell integration constitute a genuine empirical and methodological extension rather than a first-in-class discovery. Novelty is further supported by cross-validation across HCC, melanoma, and NSCLC, though the authors appropriately position the work relative to Fridman, Laumont & Nelson, and related literature.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a clear introduction (in the Main section), logical results flow from discovery through orthogonal validations and mechanism, and a comprehensive discussion that acknowledges limitations (pretreatment biopsy size, low cell counts, unverified antigen specificity). The abstract is quantitatively grounded and accurately reflects the paper. Figure captions are detailed and largely self-contained, specifying statistical tests, sample sizes, and panel contents. Minor issues include occasional dense passages with heavy acronym use (e.g., methods paragraphs on spatial clustering), some repetition between results subsections and discussion, and a few sentences that would benefit from tightening; overall the writing is publication-ready.

key_strengths: Multi-modal integration (scRNA-seq, BCR-seq, bulk RNA-seq, mIHC, spatial transcriptomics, seromics, ELISpot, ELISA) with internally consistent findings across data types
Validation across seven independent cohorts covering ~500 scRNA-seq patients, spatial data from 7, and ~1,582 survival patients spanning HCC, melanoma, and NSCLC
Isotype-resolved clonal tracking of IgG1+ PCs with evidence of tumor/lymph-node trafficking and on-treatment expansion of preexisting clones
Translationally actionable candidate biomarker (IgG1 PC signature plus anti-CTA seroreactivity) with concrete pathway targets (IL-6, TNF, ERN1, RRBP1, CD70) for combination strategies
Strong public data deposition posture (dbGaP, GEO, SRA, EGA, Zenodo) and detailed assay methods
key_concerns: Small subgroup sizes in several analyses (bulk RNA-seq 4R vs 8NR; BCR-seq 2R vs 4NR; spatial 4R vs 3NR; ELISpot essentially single patients) limit robustness
No power calculation; FDR significance thresholds vary across analyses (0.05 vs 0.2) and blinding of pathological response assessment is not described
Antigen specificity of clonally expanded PCs is not directly demonstrated (acknowledged by authors)—functional linkage of IgG1 PCs to anti-CTA antibodies remains correlative
REMARK/biomarker reporting is incomplete: no explicit pre-specification, limited patient-flow details, no multivariable adjustment in survival analyses
Causal inference is limited by observational design in the discovery cohort; survival associations rely on expression stratification without reported cutpoint justification
chief_reviewer.rationale: A rigorously triangulated, multi-cohort translational study with a credible candidate predictive biomarker for ICB response and plausible mechanistic framework; small subgroup sizes and incomplete REMARK adherence warrant minor revisions but do not undermine the core claims, placing the work at the top tier of oncology journals.
